newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends up on soy strength, long rolling.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends up on soy strength, long rolling.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled higher on spillover strength from the CBOT soy complex and after a fund rolled long positions to the May contract from the March, traders said.
"We gained after a fund rolled its longs into the May, and our gains were extended on strength in soy," a KCBT floor broker said.

New crop KCBT July wheat also gained on ideas that rains would miss key growing areas of Kansas, Colorado and Nebraska. Earlier, July had weakened on the arrival of needed rains in HRW growing regions of Texas and Oklahoma.

KCBT May wheat rose at the midsession as Rosenthal Collins, a commission house tied to large fund holdings, bear-spread 2.5 million May/March bushels at 28 to 29 cents. On Tuesday, Rosenthal did four million of the same spread.
KCBT wheat settled three to eight cents per bushel higher, with March up three at $4.22. May climbed five cents to $3.96.

Other players apart from Rosenthal included Term Commodities, which bought 1.2 million Sept 1997 bushels, traders said. Cargill Investor Services bull-spread 900,000 March/May at 27 to 29 cents and bought one million March outright.
